reasoning_content:
Now I have the exact lines:
- qgis-server's command: lines 97–119 (in file numbers: `command: >` is line 97, the `"` ending line 119)
- nginx service: `  nginx:` — find its line: from the earlier grep: qgis is 93, so nginx's `  nginx:` is probably around line 209. Line 214 is the bad volume mount. And `  tileserver:` is line 224.

Let me write a Python patcher using the python in the backend image. I'll define the new qgis command as a literal string in the file:

```yaml
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        mkdir -p /etc/postgresql-common &&
        printf '[%s]\nhost=db\nport=5432\ndbname=%s\nuser=%s\npassword=%s\nsslmode=disable\n' "$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}" "$${DB_NAME}" "$${QGIS_DB_USER}" "$${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}" > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf &&
        mkdir -p /var/www/data/qgis &&
        ln -sf /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi /var/www/data/qgis/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        rm -f /tmp/.X99-lock &&
        fc-cache &&
        /usr/bin/Xvfb :99 -ac -screen 0 1280x1024x16 +extension GLX +render -noreset >/dev/null &
        sleep 2 &&
        grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf &&
        nginx &&
        spawn-fcgi -F 2 -u www-data -g www-data -d /var/lib/qgis -P /run/qgis.pid -p 9993 -- /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        tail -f /dev/null
```

Wait — the sed line: `sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;'` — inside a `|` block scalar, backslash+4-spaces: `\    client_max_body_size 500M;` — YAML preserves this as-is. When the shell executes: sed appends "    client_max_body_size 500M;" — good, same behavior as before.

But note: inside a `|` block scalar, the line `        grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;' &&` — YAML block scalar: is it OK to have a backslash followed by a space? In YAML literal blocks, backslashes are literal. The continuation after `a` in sed's append — `\    client_max_body_size 500M;` — sed interprets `\` followed by spaces as: the append text starts after the space... Actually `sed 'a\    text'` — GNU sed: `a\` followed by a space and text on the same line → does the space become part of the text? Let me test later. The production compose uses the exact same sed in a `>` folded scalar, where `\    client...` remains as `\    client...`. Hmm wait, in a folded scalar `.../a \    client_max_body_size 500M;...` — does YAML folding turn `\    ` into `\ `? A backslash followed by multiple spaces: the YAML folding rule — "space following backslash": in folded scalars, are non-space characters preserved and runs of spaces preserved?? The exact rule (YAML 1.1/1.2): "line folding: if a non-empty line ends with a single space, the fold is replaced by a single space; otherwise the newline and all following spaces are removed." Hmm, so a run of spaces after a newline: "in a folded scalar, all line breaks are stripped... each line break (except line breaks preceding an empty line or a more-indented line) is replaced by a single space, except when the line break immediately precedes a non-space character... hmm, I don't remember exactly. Empirically, the production qgis command renders as: `grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a     client_max_body_size 500M;'` — from the inspect of the production compose earlier? I've only inspected the dev version: `grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a     client_max_body_size 500M;' &&` — yes, in the rendered CMD the backslash was... looking at the inspect output above: `grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a     client_max_body_size 500M;' &&` — hmm, the backslash seems to be gone, and there are 5 spaces? Hard to tell from that output. The inspect output showed `a \    client_max_body_size 500M;` → actually it showed: `sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;'` — I can see `a \    client` — in the earlier inspect: `|| sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;' &&` — yes, the backslash is present.

In any case — the grep guard means the sed only runs if the string isn't already present; the qgis image's /etc/nginx/nginx.conf — does it already have client_max_body_size? The image's default nginx.conf probably doesn't → the sed runs. I'll test the behavior inside a scratch container after the fix; if the sed appends garbage, I'll adjust (the qgis server_name `_` config doesn't set client_max_body_size; it's only needed for large project uploads — for GetCapabilities it's irrelevant, but keep the behavior).

For my `|` literal block: each line is preserved as-is (no folding), so the shell receives: `sed -i '/http {/a \    client_max_body_size 500M;'` — GNU sed: `a\` then `    client...`: after `a\`, when the command continues on the same line, GNU sed strips the first space? POSIX: "the text of the a command is the text after the first space following a\"... GNU sed accepts both forms; `sed 'a\    text'` → does the text become "   text" (3 spaces) or "text"? To be safe, let me quickly test in a scratch container. Actually simpler: write the sed so it doesn't use a backslash at all: `sed -i '/http {/a\    client_max_body_size 500M;'` hmm, same thing. Use a different form: `sed -i '/http {/a "    client_max_body_size 500M;"'`? GNU sed's `a` with quotes: `sed '/http {/a "text"'` works in GNU sed (quotes are stripped). Or the safest: use two -e's:
`sed -i -e '/http {/a\    client_max_body_size 500M' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf` — same backslash problem.
Test: `echo 'http {' | sed '/http {/a\    hi'`. I'll do this in a scratch container right now along with the pg_service printf.

- backend-wms: insert before `  tileserver:` (line 224):
```yaml
  backend-wms:
    build:
      context: ../backend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    image: qonnectra/backend:dev
    container_name: qonnectra_backend_wms_dev
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 --workers 4 --timeout 60 core.wsgi:application
    expose:
      - "8000"
    volumes:
      - static_volume:/app/static
      - media_volume:/app/media
    environment:
      - DEBUG=${DEBUG:-True}
      - DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=${DJANGO_SECRET_KEY}
      - DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=${DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS:-api.localhost,localhost,127.0.0.1}
      - USE_COOKIE_DOMAIN_MIDDLEWARE=${USE_COOKIE_DOMAIN_MIDDLEWARE:-True}
      - COOKIE_DOMAIN=${COOKIE_DOMAIN:-.localhost}
      - DB_NAME=${DB_NAME}
      - DB_USER=${DB_USER}
      - DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - DB_HOST=db
      - DB_PORT=5432
      - DEFAULT_SRID=${DEFAULT_SRID:-25832}
      - CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS:-https://app.localhost}
      - CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=${CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-https://api.localhost,https://app.localhost}
      - FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - QGIS_DOMAIN=${QGIS_DOMAIN:-qgis.localhost}
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - qonnectra_network
```

- nginx mount fix (line 214).

I'll do all of this with python3 inside the backend container (docker run --rm -v /workspace:/ws qonnectra/backend:dev python3). Wait — the backend image's WORKDIR is /app; run python3 with a heredoc script: `docker run --rm -v /workspace:/ws -w /ws qonnectra/backend:dev python3 - <<'PY' ...` — stdin will be the python script.

Let me carefully write the patch script.

action.command:
docker run --rm -v /workspace:/ws -w /ws qonnectra/backend:dev python3 - <<'PY'
import re
p = '/ws/deployment/docker-compose.dev.yml'
s = open(p).read()

# --- Fix 1: nginx volume mount (mount site conf, not the full main nginx.conf)
old_mount = "      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro"
new_mount = "      - ./nginx/default.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro"
assert s.count(old_mount) == 1, s.count(old_mount)
s = s.replace(old_mount, new_mount, 1)

# --- Fix 2: qgis-server command (folded-scalar heredoc bug -> explicit list)
old_cmd = """    command: >
      sh -c "
        mkdir -p /etc/postgresql-common &&
        cat > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf <<EOF
      [${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}]
      host=db
      port=5432
      dbname=${DB_NAME}
      user=${QGIS_DB_USER}
      password=${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}
      sslmode=disable
      EOF
        mkdir -p /var/www/data/qgis &&
        ln -sf /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi /var/www/data/qgis/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        rm -f /tmp/.X99-lock &&
        fc-cache &&
        /usr/bin/Xvfb :99 -ac -screen 0 1280x1024x16 +extension GLX +render -noreset >/dev/null &
        sleep 2 &&
        grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a \\    client_max_body_size 500M;' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf &&
        nginx &&
        spawn-fcgi -F 2 -u www-data -g www-data -d /var/lib/qgis -P /run/qgis.pid -p 9993 -- /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        tail -f /dev/null
      "
"""
new_cmd = """    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        mkdir -p /etc/postgresql-common &&
        printf '[%s]\\nhost=db\\nport=5432\\ndbname=%s\\nuser=%s\\npassword=%s\\nsslmode=disable\\n' "$${QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME:-qonnectra}" "$${DB_NAME}" "$${QGIS_DB_USER}" "$${QGIS_DB_PASSWORD}" > /etc/postgresql-common/pg_service.conf &&
        mkdir -p /var/www/data/qgis &&
        ln -sf /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi /var/www/data/qgis/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        rm -f /tmp/.X99-lock &&
        fc-cache &&
        /usr/bin/Xvfb :99 -ac -screen 0 1280x1024x16 +extension GLX +render -noreset >/dev/null &
        sleep 2 &&
        grep -q 'client_max_body_size' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf || sed -i '/http {/a \\    client_max_body_size 500M;' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf &&
        nginx &&
        spawn-fcgi -F 2 -u www-data -g www-data -d /var/lib/qgis -P /run/qgis.pid -p 9993 -- /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi &&
        tail -f /dev/null
"""
assert s.count(old_cmd) == 1, "qgis cmd not found: %d" % s.count(old_cmd)
s = s.replace(old_cmd, new_cmd, 1)

# --- Fix 3: add backend-wms service (referenced by nginx default.conf upstream)
wms_service = """  backend-wms:
    build:
      context: ../backend
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    image: qonnectra/backend:dev
    container_name: qonnectra_backend_wms_dev
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 --workers 4 --timeout 60 core.wsgi:application
    expose:
      - "8000"
    volumes:
      - static_volume:/app/static
      - media_volume:/app/media
    environment:
      - DEBUG=${DEBUG:-True}
      - DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=${DJANGO_SECRET_KEY}
      - DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=${DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS:-api.localhost,localhost,127.0.0.1}
      - USE_COOKIE_DOMAIN_MIDDLEWARE=${USE_COOKIE_DOMAIN_MIDDLEWARE:-True}
      - COOKIE_DOMAIN=${COOKIE_DOMAIN:-.localhost}
      - DB_NAME=${DB_NAME}
      - DB_USER=${DB_USER}
      - DB_PASSWORD=${DB_PASSWORD}
      - DB_HOST=db
      - DB_PORT=5432
      - DEFAULT_SRID=${DEFAULT_SRID:-25832}
      - CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS:-https://app.localhost}
      - CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=${CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-https://api.localhost,https://app.localhost}
      - FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY=${FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - QGIS_DOMAIN=${QGIS_DOMAIN:-qgis.localhost}
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - qonnectra_network

  tileserver:
"""
assert s.count("  tileserver:\n") == 1
s = s.replace("  tileserver:\n", wms_service, 1)

open(p, 'w').write(s)
print("patched OK")
PY
